#F1 #BrazilGP

Raining more heavily now #F1 #BrazilGP
Leclerc trying to find a way past Lawson for P7. Great drive from Lawson but from P2 on the opening lap he's had to defend the rest of the race #F1 #BrazilGP

Leclerc toughed it out and went straight onto intermediates and is up to P8 ahead of Hamilton

Antonelli told to swap positions and does move over for Russell #F1 #BrazilGP

Norris leads by 12.4s from Verstappen now - that's coming down quickly in these conditions 

Russell now all over Antonelli for P4 after stopping a lap earlier #F1 #BrazilGP
Hamilton spins on slicks approaching the pits! Somehow doesn't hit the barrier! Straight into the pits #F1 #BrazilGP
Norris pits too - everyone has to now #F1 #BrazilGP
It's raining more heavily! Russell gambles on intermediates now! Alonso and Albon also in #F1 #BrazilGP

Fair play to Norris, he is pulling away at two seconds per lap from Verstappen behind 

Hadjar defending from Antonelli for P3 #F1 #BrazilGP
This looks so tricky now. Lap times are about four seconds slower than a few laps ago. 11 laps remaining #F1 #BrazilGP
Antonelli told it will be intermediate conditions when heavier rain arrives, but it's definitely getting damp out there again with everyone on slicks #F1 #BrazilGP
You can see the rain on Lawson's onboard camera. Lap times starting to drop off with 14 laps to go #F1 #BrazilGP

Russell and Leclerc the only drivers yet to make a second stop in the top ten

And then Norris gets told there should be a few minutes of rain now, and that there could be heavier rain with six laps remaining... #F1 #BrazilGP

Into the pits comes Kimi Antonelli. He needed fresh tyres

Norris back into the lead, 7.6s ahead of Verstappen

Hadjar passes Russell for P3, with Antonelli within 5s #F1 #BrazilGP

Hadjar also pits, so didn't follow through on trying to go to the end

Antonelli leads by 7.7s but Norris is 1.4s per lap quicker #F1 #BrazilGP
Norris called in from the lead, Hadjar stays out and leads by 2.2s from Antonelli #F1 #BrazilGP
Hadjar reports it's raining. Red Bull says it's the light rain that was expected #F1 #BrazilGP

Norris told Hadjar and Antonelli look like they will try to go to the end so he'll have to pass them on track if he stops

Norris replies: "Yeah, that's fine!" #F1 #BrazilGP

Hamilton was 0.7s quicker than Norris on the last lap

Verstappen into the pits for a new set of softs, releasing Hadjar again. Does McLaren cover and bring Norris in? Hadjar might try running longer in the lead in that case... #F1 #BrazilGP
Hamilton's pit stop put him one lap down directly behind Norris, and although he's much quicker he's struggling to un-lap himself #F1 #BrazilGP
Here's our answer. Gasly in for another set of softs, and Hamilton with the same stop one lap later #F1 #BrazilGP
Hadjar told to let Verstappen through and he does. Verstappen now P2, and 8.8s behind leader Norris #F1 #BrazilGP

Someone at the FIA forgot about the 'any grid penalty over 15 places is treated the same' rule...

Huge well done to Rafael Camara. Horrible conditions for his first ever F1 qualifying session, and he did suffer a big spin and whack into the barrier which could have taken him out.

But it didn't! And he was 12th fastest in Q1 to put that Haas through and delight the locals 👏

Qualifying resuming at 4.26pm local time, FIA confirms - two minutes from now.

Cue the stampede as everyone immediately flies out into the pit lane.

Q1 key here as the result of Q1, should they finish it, will surely be used to set the whole grid if the rest of the session doesn't get done.

If qualifying cannot resume, the FIA can either:

- Reschedule for Sunday AM, as they did in 2024

or

- Use a new rule which would allow them to set the grid based on the standings.

Latter would mean Antonelli on pole and Norris on the front row, as all four drivers between them have penalties.

If they gave out Driver of the Day for qualifying, this guy would be a shoo-in 🦖

Still no sign of qualifying resuming any time soon. Bernd Maylander is back on track in the safety car but his feedback to race control is that conditions are worse than they were on his first run ⛈️

Ferrari have had to change the engine in Lewis Hamilton's car again, after his FP3 issues. More parts added to his pool means the 10-place grid penalty he planned to serve has now been upgraded to a full back-of-grid start.

He'll be starting down with Max Verstappen in Sao Paulo on Sunday.

Colton Herta will make a hastily-arranged appearance in FP1 in Brazil, as Cadillac continue to work to get him an FIA superlicence.

He’ll take over Sergio Perez’s car.

Haas have fully axed Esteban Ocon, Rafael Camara stepping in to make his F1 debut in São Paulo.

Ayao Komatsu says “private nature of closed-door” conversation that led to this point will remain private – no public explanation of what exactly happened which led to this.

Oscar Piastri did it for Lando Norris last year, Lewis Hamilton did it for Nico Rosberg in 2016, but George Russell could not find the strength to stick around for Kimi Antonelli's title part in Mexico on Sunday.

Understandable, but Mercedes celebrated their return to F1 power without a key man.

A €5,000 fine for this, which Mercedes will be picking up. The least they can do given they still cannot fix the deployment issues he has had in his car for a long time.

Russell did not attend the hearing – he had already left the circuit.
Unlike Valtteri Bottas, George Russell did not have prior permission from the FIA to skip the media pen after the race. He now has to explain to the stewards why.

Charles Leclerc says he planned on giving the position back to Lewis Hamilton on lap one, but then saw Max Verstappen got by and so he thought it was worth just waiting and seeing what the stewards made of it.

Hamilton has called for “serious talks” at Ferrari.

Esteban Ocon has rejected speculation that he was dropped by Haas in Mexico because of an incident of "physical violence".

One rumour doing the rounds claimed Ocon might have been involved in an altercation with Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu, but the Frenchman has denied that.

Speaking minutes after the end of FP1 in Mexico, during which Colton Herta secured the final superlicence point he needed to be eligible to race in F1 in 2027, Cadillac boss Marcin Budkowski said he needs to see "more" from Valtteri Bottas in the coming weeks if the Finn is to save his seat 🗣️🚨
